summaries.gardner: BeOne fits several Rule Breaker traits: it is a top dog in the BTK-inhibitor class with a sustainable edge from BRUKINSA's head-to-head win over Imbruvica, backed by a founder CEO and smart partners such as Amgen. It is weaker on consumer brand recognition and the stock's momentum is only moderate, while some commentators call it expensive at about 60x trailing earnings, which Gardner would see as a plus.
summaries.buffett: Buffett would admire the high gross margins (87-90%) but would struggle with the lack of a long consistent earnings record (first annual profit in FY2025), dependence on one drug for ~73% of sales and the hard-to-predict science and regulation of biotech. At roughly 60x trailing earnings there is no margin of safety in his sense.
summaries.munger: Munger would credit the hard-to-copy in-house clinical machine and founder-led long-term thinking, but inverting reveals several failure paths: one-product concentration, US-China geopolitics, US drug-price reform and next-generation BTK competition. It is outside the simple, predictable 'too hard' filter for most generalists.
summaries.lynch: In Lynch's terms BeOne is a fast grower (revenue up 40% in FY2025, 2026 guided ~25% higher) with a simple story: BRUKINSA keeps taking BTK share while new drugs launch. The P/E of about 60 trailing and high-30s forward is above its expected earnings growth, and insiders are selling rather than buying.
summaries.fisher: BeOne scores well on Fisher's points for R&D that produces results (BRUKINSA, TEVIMBRA, sonrotoclax all discovered in-house), a deep pipeline for when current products mature and strong commercial execution in the US. Profit margins are only now emerging, and heavy share issuance over the years is a minus.
summaries.graham: BeOne fails almost all of Graham's defensive-investor tests: it has no ten-year earnings record, pays no dividend, and trades far above 15x average earnings and the 22.5 P/E-times-P/B limit. Its only pass is a strong balance sheet with about $5.1B of cash against $1.07B of debt.
summaries.thiel: BeOne has a proprietary edge (best-in-class BTK data, in-house global clinical operations) and a strong founding team with a secret few saw in 2010: global-quality drugs developed from China at speed and low cost. But BTK inhibitors are a contested market rather than a monopoly, and its technology is better rather than ten times better.
summaries.gerstner: Gerstner would like the operating leverage story: revenue growing 25-30% with GAAP operating income guided to $1.0-1.1B in 2026 after losses, and strong free cash flow emerging. Valuation near 60x trailing earnings and exposure to US-China policy risk would be weighed against that inflection.
summaries.druckenmiller: Earnings are accelerating and estimates are rising (2026 guidance raised in August, Q2 EPS of $2.05 per ADS beat $1.40 consensus), which suits Druckenmiller's focus on improving fundamentals. Macro and liquidity matter little to the drug business, but geopolitical and pricing-policy catalysts cut both ways.
summaries.smith: Smith would value the 87-90% gross margins and growing free cash flow ($941.7M in FY2025), but returns on capital are only just turning positive after years of losses, and the business depends heavily on one drug with finite patent life. The valuation is not cheap enough to satisfy 'don't overpay'.
summaries.greenblatt: On the Magic Formula BeOne ranks poorly: its earnings yield (operating income versus enterprise value) is only around 2-3%, and return on capital is only now becoming positive. It is a growth story rather than a good-and-cheap business.
summaries.akre: Akre's three legs are mixed: the business is becoming a good compounder with high gross margins, the founder-led management has executed well, but the reinvestment leg is unproven because R&D returns beyond BRUKINSA are still to be shown. Steady dilution and insider selling detract.
summaries.pabrai: BeOne does not fit Dhandho: it is not a simple, distressed business priced for heads-I-win, tails-I-don't-lose-much. Its prospects are good but the price already reflects much of the growth.
summaries.wood: BeOne is an innovative oncology developer with a BTK degrader and new modalities, but it is not a leader in ARK's core platforms such as multiomic sequencing or AI-driven drug discovery. Its addressable market grows steadily rather than many-fold.
summaries.ackman: Ackman would like the high-margin, increasingly predictable cash generation and the dominant BRUKINSA franchise with a pricing-power-like gross margin. However, biotech pipeline and policy risk make it less simple and predictable than his usual targets, and there is no obvious activist angle.
summaries.sleep: Nick Sleep's scale-economics-shared model fits partly: BeOne's low-cost clinical development and China operations could let it price more affordably and reinvest, but drug pricing is mostly set by payers and patents, not by passing scale savings to customers. Its 10-20-year position depends on pipeline success.
summaries.valentine: Valentine would appreciate the huge, painful problem (cancer) and a team that built a global company from scratch, but BeOne is now a large public company rather than an early-stage market-creating opportunity. Its market is large and growing.
summaries.nash: BeOne passes many Nash quality checks (revenue growth over 25%, more than twice as much cash as debt, revenue growing faster than expenses, low 1.7% short interest), scoring about 80 on his 13 categories. But it hits an instant kill on operating margin below 20%, sits partly in the 'Chinese company' avoid zone, has heavy insider selling, and its DCF and PEG do not support today's price.

momentum.evidence: The ADS rose from about $310 in October 2025 to about $353 in October 2026 (+14%, +16.6% year to date by early October), a solid but not exceptional gain.

g4.evidence: Founder-led by John Oyler and co-founder Xiaodong Wang, with Amgen as a long-time strategic shareholder and partner and specialist funds among its backers.

g6.evidence: At about 62x trailing and 39x forward earnings some commentators call it expensive, though the consensus target (~$405-435) sits above the price.

simple.evidence: The core story (sell more BRUKINSA, launch new cancer drugs) is simple, but judging clinical trials and drug pricing needs specialist knowledge.

b2.evidence: BeOne lost money every year until a first annual net profit of $286.9M in FY2025.

integrity.evidence: Disclosure is detailed and guidance has been raised and met, but large stock-based pay, years of share issuance and heavy insider selling (about $192.6M in the past three months) weigh against owner alignment.

b6.evidence: It has grown mainly through in-house discovery (BRUKINSA, TEVIMBRA, sonrotoclax) rather than large acquisitions.

roic.evidence: After years of large losses, returns on capital are only just turning positive (FY2025 net margin 5.4%), so there is no high, consistent record.

fcf.evidence: FY2025 free cash flow was $941.7M, more than three times GAAP net income of $286.9M.

b10.evidence: It retains no profits historically (accumulated deficit), but billions of reinvested capital built a franchise now worth about $41B in market value.

safety.evidence: At about $353 per ADS (roughly $41B market cap) and ~62x trailing earnings, the price is not well below a conservative value.

fairprice.evidence: A forward P/E near 39 against expected earnings growth of roughly 25-27% a year is full but not extreme for its growth and quality.

mu5.evidence: It could be hurt by BRUKINSA concentration (~73% of sales), fixed-duration CLL regimens, Jaypirca, US price controls and US-China policy.

reinvest.evidence: It reinvests heavily ($2.15B R&D in FY2025) with a credible pipeline (sonrotoclax, BTK degrader, CDK4 inhibitor), but returns beyond BRUKINSA are unproven.

ly2.evidence: A clear fast grower: revenue up 40.2% in FY2025 and guided to $6.6-6.8B for 2026.

ly3.evidence: The trailing P/E of about 62 and forward P/E of about 39 exceed the expected earnings growth rate.

runway.evidence: New indications (first-line MCL for BRUKINSA), new launches (sonrotoclax, TEVIMBRA in Japan and HER2+ GEA) and solid-tumour entries give years of growth runway.

ly7.evidence: Insiders sold about $192.6M in the past three months with no purchases, and diluted ADSs rose from 83.5M (FY2020) to 115.8M (Q2 2026).

ly8.evidence: It is widely covered (around 30 analysts) and about 48.6% institutionally owned.

fi2.evidence: It is building successors to BRUKINSA, including sonrotoclax and the tacabrutideg BTK degrader, while BRUKINSA is still growing.

fi3.evidence: Internal R&D produced BRUKINSA, TEVIMBRA and sonrotoclax (FDA accelerated approval in 2026), all now commercial.

fi4.evidence: It built a US commercial team that grew BRUKINSA US sales to $2.8B in FY2025 (+45%), overtaking Calquence and Imbruvica globally.

longterm.evidence: Management absorbed years of multi-billion losses to build global R&D and manufacturing (e.g. Hopewell, NJ plant and a $300M expansion).

gr1.evidence: Market value is about $41B and FY2025 revenue was $5.34B.

ni10.evidence: FY2025 was its first profitable year.

gr4.evidence: BeOne has never paid a dividend.

eps10.evidence: EPS was negative for most of the last ten years, so there is no ten-year EPS growth record.

gr6.evidence: The price is about 62x trailing earnings and far above 15x average earnings, which were negative.

gr7.evidence: P/E of ~62 times P/B of ~7.9 (about $41B market cap vs $5.17B equity) far exceeds 22.5.

th1.evidence: BRUKINSA is measurably better than ibrutinib in ALPINE, but not ten times better than Calquence or Jaypirca.

timing.evidence: Its 2010 bet on China-based global development has matured into profitability just as its BTK franchise peaks and new launches start.

th3.evidence: It started in China oncology and then broke into the large US/EU BTK market, now expanding into solid tumours, but it was never a monopolist in a small market.

team.evidence: Co-founders John Oyler (CEO since 2010) and scientist Xiaodong Wang have built a $5B+ revenue oncology company from scratch.

th5.evidence: It has its own commercial forces in the US, Europe, China and 40+ markets rather than relying on partners.

durable.evidence: BRUKINSA's exclusivity runs into the 2030s, so a 10-20 year position depends on successors such as sonrotoclax and the BTK degrader succeeding.

th7.evidence: Its in-house, China-anchored global clinical model was a contrarian insight, though rivals are now copying China sourcing of drug candidates.

trend.evidence: It benefits from rising global cancer prevalence and China's rise in drug innovation, not from a tech platform shift like AI.

dr1.evidence: Guidance was raised in August 2026 to $6.6-6.8B revenue and $1.0-1.1B GAAP operating income, and Q2 EPS of $2.05/ADS beat the $1.40 consensus.

dr2.evidence: Sonrotoclax launch, BRUKINSA first-line MCL filings and the BTK degrader filing could make it look better, but these are widely expected.

dr4.evidence: Drug demand is largely independent of rates and the economy, but tariffs, FX and US policy toward China-linked companies are headwinds.

dr6.evidence: Catalysts include a 2H 2026 FDA decision on TEVIMBRA in HER2+ gastric cancer, BRUKINSA first-line MCL submissions and a possible BTK-degrader filing in R/R CLL.

dr7.evidence: Fundamentals are improving fast, but single-product concentration and geopolitical risk argue against a very large concentrated position.

gm.evidence: GAAP gross margin was 87.3% of product sales in FY2025 and about 90% in Q2 2026.

fcfyield.evidence: FY2025 free cash flow of $941.7M on a ~$41B market cap is a ~2.3% yield, modest but rising quickly.

gb2.evidence: Operating income of roughly $0.9B over the last year against an enterprise value near $37B is only about 2-3%.

pa2.evidence: The business is not in a setback; revenue and profits are growing strongly.

pa4.evidence: Net cash of about $4B and growing cash flow limit downside, but a premium valuation and policy risk mean permanent loss is possible.

wo1.evidence: It is an oncology drug company, not a leader in AI, robotics, energy storage, blockchain or multiomic sequencing.

wo2.evidence: Unit costs fall with scale (gross margin up from ~77% in FY2020 to ~90% in Q2 2026), but this does not open big new demand as with Wright's-law technologies.

wo3.evidence: It combines small molecules, antibodies, protein degraders and ADCs, but these are drug modalities rather than ARK's innovation platforms.

wo4.evidence: Its addressable oncology markets are large but grow steadily, not many-fold within five years.

ac3.evidence: Demand is insulated from commodities and rates, but FX (RMB, EUR), tariffs and drug-pricing policy affect results.

ns1.evidence: Its founding aim is more affordable medicines and its low-cost development supports that, but US pricing of BRUKINSA is not markedly below rivals.

ns4.evidence: A broader commercial portfolio and pipeline should strengthen it, but BRUKINSA's patent clock and new BTK competitors make this uncertain.

va2.evidence: It treats cancers such as CLL, lymphoma and gastric cancer, a large and painful problem for millions of patients.

tn1.evidence: It sells into the secular growth of oncology spending, but that is not an AI/energy/robotics-type infrastructure trend.

tn2.evidence: Some still see it as a 'Chinese biotech', while it has become a Swiss-domiciled global oncology company with most sales in the US.

tn3.evidence: It is a large cap, not a startup or commodity producer, but its heavy China R&D and manufacturing footprint puts it near Nash's 'Chinese companies' avoid zone.

tn4.evidence: It passes all three: revenue grew every year to $5.34B, it was profitable in FY2025, and cash of $5.10B exceeds $1.07B debt.

tn5.evidence: Cash has exceeded debt every quarter and FY2025 and H1 2026 operating cash flow were strongly positive ($1.13B and $664M), but quarter-by-quarter FCF for early 2025 was not verified.

tn6.evidence: Revenue grew 40.2% in FY2025 and about 32% in H1 2026.

tn7.evidence: FY2025 revenue growth of 40.2% plus a 17.6% FCF margin ($941.7M/$5,343M) gives about 58.

tn8.evidence: In FY2025 revenue grew 40.2% while R&D plus SG&A grew about 11.7% ($4.23B vs $3.78B).

tn9.evidence: It fails the operating-margin test: FY2025 GAAP operating margin was 8.4% and 2026 guidance implies about 16%, both below 20%.

tn10.evidence: It faces US drug-pricing reform, tariff and BIOSECURE-style China legislation risk, and patent litigation over its products.

tn11.evidence: It provides cancer drugs like BRUKINSA that help patients with blood cancers live longer with fewer side effects, and charges per prescription paid by insurers; doctors choose it for better head-to-head data.

tn13.evidence: Total about 80: cash 10, growth 10, operating margin 5, short interest (1.7%) 10, institutions (48.6%) 5, revenue faster than expenses 10, 5-year return vs S&P 0, moat 5, CEO 5, pricing power 5, trend 5, culture 5, talent 5.

tn14.evidence: Revenue grew every year and margins expanded, but free cash flow was negative until FY2025 (e.g. -$633.3M in FY2024).

tn15.evidence: Operating income ($575M in H1 2026) far exceeds interest costs on $1.07B debt, current ratio is about 3.4, and liabilities of $4.0B are below equity of $5.17B.

tn18.evidence: Oyler is a founder CEO of 16 years with a strong growth record, but he has been selling (reportedly over $62M since June 2026) rather than buying on the open market.

tn20.evidence: Q2 2026 EPS of $2.05/ADS beat the $1.40 consensus and revenue beat, but a full multi-quarter beat record was not verified.

tn21.evidence: Insiders sold about $192.6M of stock in three months, including the CEO, while the shares traded near highs.

tn22.evidence: It has $5.3B of revenue, positive earnings and free cash flow, and no longer depends on share sales to fund itself.

tn24.evidence: An EV of about $37B at roughly 30x trailing free cash flow implies mid-teens growth, below the 25-30% it is currently delivering, but margins must keep rising to justify it.

tn25.evidence: Nash's 3-year average FCF margin is negative (losses in FY2023-FY2024), so his DCF at 12% gives a value well below $353 per ADS.

tn26.evidence: A forward P/E of about 39 against ~25-27% expected EPS growth gives a PEG near 1.5, above 1.
